content.user_title: Dispatch Independent Tasks Across Parallel Agents
content.value_statement: Sequential investigation slows work when failures have unrelated causes. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code delegate focused tasks and verify combined results.
actual_capabilities: Identifies whether tasks are independent enough for parallel work.
Groups failures by test file, subsystem, or problem domain.
Creates focused agent assignments with scope, goals, constraints, and expected output.
Dispatches one agent for each independent problem domain.
Guides conflict review, full-suite testing, and final integration.
limitations: It is unsuitable when tasks share state or depend on earlier results.
It requires an environment that supports multiple concurrent agents.
It does not guarantee that agent fixes are correct.
It requires a final human or agent-led integration review.

use_cases.title: Triage Independent Test Failures
use_cases.description: Assign unrelated failing test files to separate agents and combine verified fixes.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers maintaining large test suites

use_cases.title: Coordinate Subsystem Repairs
use_cases.description: Delegate independent frontend, backend, and tooling problems with clear ownership boundaries.

use_cases.title: Accelerate Repository Maintenance
use_cases.description: Run separate documentation, testing, and cleanup tasks concurrently when files do not overlap.

prompt_templates.title: Check Task Independence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these tasks: {{tasks}}. Identify which tasks are independent and explain which ones must remain sequential.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment before using parallel agents

prompt_templates.title: Create Focused Assignments
prompt_templates.prompt: Group these failures by root-cause domain: {{failures}}. Create one focused agent assignment for each independent group.

prompt_templates.title: Dispatch Parallel Investigations
prompt_templates.prompt: Dispatch parallel agents for {{independent_tasks}}. Give each agent a scope, goal, constraints, evidence, and required summary.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced execution in a multi-agent environment

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Parallel Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these agent results: {{results}}. Detect conflicts, verify assumptions, run relevant tests, and prepare one integrated conclusion.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated test files fail after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates three focused assignments, dispatches them concurrently, and requests a root-cause summary and verification result from each agent.

output_examples.input: Two agents changed the same shared utility while fixing separate features.
output_examples.output: The assistant flags the overlap, pauses integration, compares both assumptions, and recommends a coordinated review before running the full test suite.

output_examples.input: Documentation, unit tests, and dependency cleanup affect separate files.
output_examples.output: The assistant delegates each task independently, reviews every summary, checks changed files for overlap, and verifies the combined repository state.

best_practices: Confirm that tasks have no shared state or sequential dependency before dispatch.
Give each agent a narrow scope, complete context, explicit constraints, and a required output.
Review all changes together and run the full relevant test suite before integration.
anti_patterns: Do not parallelize failures that may share one root cause.
Do not let multiple agents edit the same files without coordination.
Do not accept agent summaries without checking changes and verification results.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when two or more tasks are independent, have clear boundaries, and can proceed without shared state.

faq.question: Can it handle related test failures?
faq.answer: Investigate related failures together first because one fix may resolve several failures.

faq.question: Does it run agents concurrently?
faq.answer: It instructs supported AI environments to dispatch concurrent tasks. Actual concurrency depends on the available agent tools.

faq.question: What context should each agent receive?
faq.answer: Provide the relevant files, errors, expected behavior, scope limits, and required final summary.

faq.question: How are conflicting changes handled?
faq.answer: Review changed files for overlap, compare assumptions, resolve conflicts, and rerun the full relevant test suite.

faq.question: Does parallel dispatch replace final verification?
faq.answer: No. Review every result, check for conflicts, and verify the integrated changes before acceptance.
